verdict.text: The change pins all three `uses:` lines in `action.yml` and all six in `knowledge-audit.yml` to the commit SHAs the plan names, each with its version as a comment.
It also adds both files to `test_every_action_is_pinned_by_commit_sha`.
Each SHA matches its upstream tag, and each action now runs at a single version across the repo.
Nothing blocks.
Diff against HEAD: `action.yml`, `.github/workflows/knowledge-audit.yml` and `tests/scripts/test_workflows.py`, nothing else.
r3 (judgment): I resolved each tag with `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/TAG`.
checkout v7.0.1 = 3d3c42e5…, setup-uv v10.2.0 = c18668ad…, upload-artifact v7.0.2 = cf430e03…, download-artifact v8.0.2 = 90008…8333.
All four match.
v8.0.2 and v7.0.2 are each repo's latest release.
Grepping every `uses:` under `action.yml` and `.github/workflows/` shows one SHA per action.
Upgrade risk: I read the release notes for the major versions skipped.
setup-uv v7 to v10 changes cache defaults, the manifest format and `server-url`.
Both files set only `enable-cache: false`, so none of that affects them.
upload-artifact v7 and download-artifact v8 keep the `name`/`path` inputs.
v8's digest-mismatch check now fails the run by default, which is the safer behaviour.
checkout keeps `fetch-depth` and `persist-credentials`.
r1/r2: the test regex requires `owner/repo@<40 hex> # vX.Y.Z` at the end of each `uses:` line, and `assert lines` guards against an empty match.
I checked by hand that a tag ref and a SHA with no comment both fail the regex.
r1's `-k ... and action` selects all four parametrized cases, including `action.yml`, as the builder said.
r2 selects `knowledge-audit.yml`.
Docs: the `@v4` examples in `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md` are readable tags on purpose, and the plan puts them out of scope.
No doc or docstring now says something false.
`loopctl gate stamp`: lint, format, tests, integration, r1 and r2 all pass.
None.
The new pins run on Node 24, which needs Actions runner 2.327.1 or later.
That only matters for consumers on old self-hosted runners.
GitHub-hosted runners already qualify.
